Modified assessment using the Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey (SLOOS) as context:

- Statement takeaways: Moderate expansion, robust job gains, low unemployment, but inflation still elevated; policy tightened to 5.25–5.50% and balance-sheet runoff continues; FOMC highlights that tighter credit conditions will weigh on activity, hiring, and inflation.
- SLOOS (July 2023) confirms broad-based credit tightening and softer demand: Banks tightened standards and, in many cases, terms across C&I (including syndicated, investment-grade and below-investment-grade firms), commercial real estate (construction, land development, nonfarm nonresidential, multifamily), residential real estate (GSE-eligible, jumbo, government, QM and non-QM), HELOCs, and consumer credit (credit cards and auto). Banks reported weaker demand (including for subprime mortgages) and expected further tightening ahead. Reported drivers include a weaker economic outlook, reduced risk tolerance, higher funding costs/liquidity concerns, and deterioration in collateral values.
- Implications: SLOOS corroborates and amplifies the FOMC’s warning that credit conditions will weigh on growth and hiring, and it adds downside risk for smaller firms, CRE-exposed sectors, and consumer spending. While fundamentals remain somewhat positive, the SLOOS tilt pulls the overall tone from slightly positive toward modestly negative.
